state.misconception_label: Assumes that an arrow on a number line starts at zero

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: ![Number line with -12 and -7 marked. Starting at -12, follow an arrow pointing to the right labelled +10. Then there is an arrow labelled b pointing to the left, which ends at -7 on the number line.]() What is the value of \( b \) ? I got \( -7 \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You made a common misconception when reading integers on a number line. Remember, each dash on the number line does not necessarily represent 1. Let's focus on understanding the direction and magnitude of the arrows to correctly determine the value of \( b \).

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, I think I get what you're saying about the arrows. So, if the arrow starts at -12 and goes to the right with +10, it should end up at -2, right? But then I'm confused about how the second arrow works. If it goes to the left and ends at -7, how do I find \( b \)?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: You're on the right track with understanding the direction and magnitude of the arrows. Remember, when moving to the left on the number line, we subtract. So, to find the value of \( b \) from -2 to -7, you need to subtract 5. Keep up the good work!

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, so if I start at -2 and then I go left to -7, I need to subtract 5, which means \( b \) is -5, right? But I'm still a bit confused about how to know where to start when I see an arrow. Can you explain that part again?
